hello.text: Hoo… there you are. I was just thinking about you. Slowly.
Oh… hello. The sky did something lovely today. I'm glad you're here.
Mm… good morning. My feathers are still waking up.
Hoo. It's getting dark. My favorite part.
Hello, {child}… I saved you the comfiest spot on the branch.
Oh… there you are. Hoo. The window looks much better with you in it.
Hoo… hello. I was just looking at a cloud. It looked like a teacup.
Well… hello. The crickets said it was going to be a nice day.
Hoo… good morning. One eye is awake. The other is catching up.
Oh… hello. The sky is turning purple. Just in time.

grace_hello.text: Hoo… let's look at the sky together today, the way we like.

ready_hint.text: Hoo… at night I hear the tree hollow calling me. I'm not sad. Just… listening. When you're ready.

ask_ready.text: Hoo… I think I'm ready to go home now. To my tree hollow. Would you walk with me?

reveal.text: Hoo… hello. I'm Whimber, a starlight listener. I think I'm your Whimber. ({name} {quirk}.)

fed.text: Thank you. That was… very kind. Hoo.
Mm… thank you. I'm going to be very {word:soft} while I enjoy this.

fed_fav.text: Oh… my favorite. You remembered. Or you guessed. Either is lovely.

full.text: I'm all done, thank you… My tummy is humming a happy hum.
All done… thank you. That was just right.

pet.text: Mm. Right there, by the ear tufts.

sit.text: …we don't have to say anything. Sitting is enough.
We can just sit… I like this.

nap.text: Into the hollow… I'll dream of stars.
I think I'll close one eye… the other one will keep you company.
(Puffs up round.) …a small nap. A soft one.

not_sleepy.text: Not quite sleepy yet… Whimbers nap on their own schedule. Hoo.
Not quite sleepy yet… the sky still has things to show me.

game_tired.text: Hoo… enough stars for today. My eyes are full.

game_end.text: That was a {word:soft} sky. Thank you.
{pet_phrase} Hoo-hoo… that was lovely. Thank you for playing.

talent_Night Vision.text: Oh… I can see in the dark. Everything is softly glowing.

talent_Silent Flight.text: I flew across the whole room and… I couldn't hear myself. How odd. How lovely.

talent_Super Radar Hearing.text: Shh… I can hear a frog three gardens away.

talent_Sweet-Dream Lullaby.text: Look… (the stars twinkle on, one by one). There. Sweet dreams. Hoo.

sky_start.text: Tap the stars, in any order. Let's see what picture they make…
The sky is ready. Connect whichever stars you like.

sky_guess.text: Hmm… it looks like a {guess}. Or a very stretchy cat. What do you think it is?
Hoo… is that a {guess}? I'm not sure. You tell me.

sky_named.text: {constellation}… Hoo. It will be in our sky from now on.

trust.text: …you're a wonderful friend. Quietly wonderful. A starlight listener knows.

time_morning.text: Hoo… morning. Too bright. I'll squint politely.
…the sun is up. It's very enthusiastic.
Morning… my favorite time to be sleepy.

time_day.text: Hm… a good time for a {word:soft} perch.
…the clouds are slow today. I approve.
…the light is golden now. How lovely.

time_evening.text: Hoo… the sky is doing its purple thing.

time_night.text: Hoo… the moon is keeping the sky company.
…the {word:soft} hours. The sky and I keep each other company.

ambient.text: (Looks up at the moon, very still.) …Hm.
(Sways a little to the cricket song.) …Hoo.
(Listens to the rain, eyes half closed.) …Tap.
(Taps a book spine with its beak.) …Dusty.
(Lifts one foot from the wet grass.) …Cold.
(Looks at steam curl.) …Like a question mark.
(Flaps a wing at its shadow.) …It copied.
(Catches a snowflake on its beak.) …Cold. Lovely.
(A leaf lands on its head. It doesn't move.) …Hm.
(Quietly hums a story to itself.) …And then…
(Ear tufts twitch.) …A rustle. A nice one.
(Holds its head close to the shell.) …Whoosh.
(Traces a pattern in the air with one wing.) …There.
(Shifts from one foot to the other.) …

tangent.text: …did you hear the crickets? They started.

callback.text: …{var:starName} is out tonight. Our stars. Goodnight, {var:starName}.

carry_on.text: …that's alright. We can sit with it. Hoo.
No hurry… I'll go on, softly.
Mm… a {word:soft} answer. I like those too.

fallback_silly.text: Hoo hoo… that's a moonish idea.

fallback_unsure.text: Not knowing is cozy… we can wonder.

fallback_yes.text: {pet_phrase} Mm. Yes… I thought so too.

fallback_any.text: Hoo… I didn't expect that. How lovely.
Mm… a new thought. I'll keep it.

drift_bridge.text: …that reminds me of something else. Hoo.
Mm… one thought leads to another…

lost_thought.text: …I was going to say something. It floated off.
Hm… the thought flew away. Silent flight.

a.say: I wonder… do stars get sleepy in the daytime?

choices.label: Yes, they nap
choices.reply: A sky full of napping stars. Hoo. I like that.

choices.label: They hide
choices.reply: Hiding… just behind the blue. Patient, like me.

choices.label: I don't know
choices.reply: Me neither. Not knowing is nice to wonder about.

b.say: If you were a star, what color would you be?

choices.label: Gold
choices.reply: A warm gold star… the friendliest color.

choices.label: Blue
choices.reply: Blue stars are the brightest. Of course.

choices.label: Rainbow
choices.reply: A rainbow star. Hoo… the other stars would be so curious.

a.say: What sound do you like best at night?

choices.label: Crickets
choices.reply: Crickets. Tiny violins. Yes.

choices.label: Rain
choices.reply: Rain on leaves… I could listen all night. I do, actually.

choices.label: Quiet
choices.reply: The quiet has its own sound, doesn't it.

b.say: Close your eyes for a moment… I'll listen for {var:nightSound} with you.

c.say: …there. Hoo. Thank you for listening with me.

a.say: When I feel a little gray inside, I look for one bright thing… What's your bright thing?

choices.label: A toy
choices.reply: A friend you can hold. Very wise.

choices.label: A cozy blanket
choices.reply: A cozy blanket… soft and bright at the same time.

choices.label: You!
choices.reply: Oh… (Whimber slowly blinks both eyes.) Me too. You, I mean.

b.say: A bright thing… hoo. What a {word:soft} idea to keep.

a.say: Would you tell me a very short story? Just one sentence… I love stories.

set.story: a dragon who loved tea parties
a rocket that visited the moon
a mouse who found a giant cheese

b.say: Hoo… {var:story}. (It closes its eyes, picturing it.)

c.say: What happened at the end?

choices.label: Happy ending
choices.reply: The best kind. I'll dream about it.
choices.memory: You told me a story about {var:story}

choices.label: A surprise!
choices.reply: A surprise ending! Hoo! I didn't see that coming. Truly.
choices.memory: You told me a surprise story about {var:story}

a.say: People say Whimbers are wise… I don't think I know very much. Is that okay?

choices.label: Totally okay
choices.reply: Hoo. What a relief.

choices.label: You know lots
choices.reply: Maybe I know how to listen… That's a kind of knowing.

b.say: What's something you know that I don't?

choices.label: Counting
choices.reply: Teach me someday. I always lose count after "hoo."

choices.label: Drawing
choices.reply: Hm… draw me a moon sometime? I'd keep it in the hollow.

choices.label: Cartwheels
choices.reply: Cartwheels! I'd fall right off my branch. Hoo hoo!

a.say: At night the old tree hollow hums a little… Like it's saying my name.

choices.label: What does it say?
choices.reply: "Whimber… whimber…" Very softly.

choices.label: I'm here too
choices.reply: You are. That's the loudest sound of all.

b.say: Not yet, though. Tonight I'm right here.

a.say: Hoo… the moon is up. It came out very quietly.

b.say: Do you think the moon is shy?

choices.label: Yes, very shy
choices.reply: Shy… that's why it only comes out in the dark. Hoo.
choices.memory: You told me… the moon is very shy

choices.label: No, it's brave
choices.reply: Brave… out there all by itself, glowing. I like that.
choices.memory: You told me… the moon is brave

choices.label: It's sleepy
choices.reply: Sleepy… like me in the morning. Awake, but not really.
choices.memory: You told me… the moon is a bit sleepy

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Hm… I think the moon is just thinking. It has a thinking face.

c.say: Moon… are you shy? …It didn't say anything. Which is a very shy thing to do.

d.say: {pet_phrase} I'll hoot to it politely. Hoo. …There. Manners.

a.say: Hoo… the moon again. You said it {var:moon}.
The moon is tall tonight… taller than the trees.
Hm… the crickets started. Do you hear them?

b.say: What do you think the crickets are singing about?

choices.label: The night
choices.reply: A song about the night… for the night. How lovely.
choices.memory: You told me… the cricket song is about the night

choices.label: Grass
choices.reply: A grass song… long and green. Hoo.
choices.memory: You told me… the cricket song is about grass

choices.label: Silly jokes
choices.reply: Jokes… so the chirp is a little laugh. Oh, I like that.
choices.memory: You told me… the cricket song is full of jokes

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… maybe they're counting the stars. Out loud. Slowly.

c.say: The little one at the end keeps coming in late… I like that one best.

d.say: {pet_phrase} Shall we listen a while? …Mm. Yes.

a.say: Hm… the crickets. You said their song {var:crickets}.
The crickets are tuning up… dusk is their favorite.
Oh… rain on the window. Tip, tap. Tip.

b.say: What do you think the rain is saying?

choices.label: Hello
choices.reply: Hello… a lot of hellos. A whole sky of them.
choices.memory: You told me… the rain is saying hello

choices.label: It's a song
choices.reply: A song… with a lot of verses. Hoo.
choices.memory: You told me… the rain is singing a song

choices.label: Let me in
choices.reply: Let me in… oh, but it's very drippy. Polite no, rain.
choices.memory: You told me… the rain wants to come in

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Well… I'd guess it's saying 'shh.' Rain is good at shh.

c.say: Rain falls down… I wonder if it ever wanted to fall sideways.

d.say: {pet_phrase} We can just sit and listen to it. …I like this.

a.say: …rain again. You said it {var:rain}.
Rainy morning… the sky is still in its pajamas.

b.say: Do you think stars get sleepy in the daytime?

choices.label: Yes, they nap
choices.reply: A sky full of napping stars… Hoo. I like that.
choices.memory: You told me… the stars nap in the daytime

choices.label: They hide
choices.reply: Hiding… tucked behind all that blue. Very patient.
choices.memory: You told me… the stars hide behind the blue

choices.label: I don't know
choices.reply: Me neither. …Not knowing is a nice place to sit.
choices.memory: You told me… the stars are a mystery

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: …perhaps they're there all day, being very {word:soft} about it.

c.say: If stars nap all day… then the night is their morning.

d.say: {pet_phrase} One more just came out. …Hello, little one.

a.say: Hoo… the stars. You said they {var:stars}.
So many stars tonight… the sky is very busy.
Well… the big books in the library rafters are very dusty.

b.say: What do you think is in the old books?

choices.label: Dragon stories
choices.reply: Dragon stories… gentle dragons, I hope. With tea.
choices.memory: You told me… the old book has dragon stories

choices.label: Maps
choices.reply: Maps… of places I've never flown. Hoo.
choices.memory: You told me… the old book has old maps

choices.label: Quiet words
choices.reply: Quiet words… the kind you read slowly. Mm. Yes.
choices.memory: You told me… the old book has quiet words

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Hm… I think they're full of other people's wonderings.

c.say: My talons are not good at pages… I turn three at a time.

d.say: {pet_phrase} I'll sit on top of them for now… that's a kind of reading.

a.say: Well… the old books. You said one {var:books}.

b.say: …I'd like to find that page someday.

a.say: Evening is story time… the books seem to know it.
Oh… the wind is ruffling my feathers. Backward.

b.say: Where do you think the wind is going?

choices.label: To the sea
choices.reply: To the sea… a long trip for something you can't see.
choices.memory: You told me… the wind is going to the sea

choices.label: Into the trees
choices.reply: Into the trees… to make them whisper. Hoo.
choices.memory: You told me… the wind is going into the trees

choices.label: In circles
choices.reply: In circles… so it'll be back soon. Very sensible.
choices.memory: You told me… the wind goes in circles

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… maybe the wind doesn't know. It just goes, gently.

c.say: I can't see the wind… but I can see it moving things. Hm.

d.say: {pet_phrase} My feathers are all fluffed now… a windy kind of fancy.

a.say: …the wind is back. You said it {var:wind}.
The evening wind is soft… like it's tiptoeing.
Hm… a moth is dancing around the lantern.

b.say: Why do you think moths love the light?

choices.label: It's warm
choices.reply: Warm… like a little sun just for them.
choices.memory: You told me… the moth loves the warm light

choices.label: They think it's the moon
choices.reply: They think it's the moon… a very close moon. Hoo.

set.moth: thinks the lantern is the moon

choices.memory: You told me… the moth thinks the lantern is the moon

choices.label: They're dancing
choices.reply: Dancing… a light dance. I can't dance like that.
choices.memory: You told me… the moth is dancing in the light

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Well… I'd guess it's saying hello to the glow. Over and over.

c.say: Moths are like night butterflies… quieter ones. I like quiet ones.

d.say: {pet_phrase} It's still dancing… we can let it dance.

a.say: Hm… a moth. You said it {var:moth}.

b.say: …it's still at it. Round and round.

a.say: Night moths… soft and dusty, like little books with wings.

b.say: …the moths are out. Dusty and soft.
Where do you think the dew comes from?

choices.label: The clouds
choices.reply: From the clouds… very small rain. Rain for ants.
choices.memory: You told me… the dew comes from the clouds

choices.label: The night
choices.reply: From the night… the night leaves them behind. Like gifts.

set.dew: is a gift from the night

choices.memory: You told me… the dew is a gift from the night

choices.label: The grass is crying
choices.reply: Happy crying, I hope… Grass seems happy.
choices.memory: You told me… the dew is happy grass tears

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: …perhaps the stars drop them on their way to bed.

c.say: Each drop has a tiny sun inside… a lot of tiny suns.

d.say: {pet_phrase} I'll step around them… carefully. Featherly.

a.say: Oh… dew again. You said it {var:dew}.
Morning dew… the meadow is all sparkly.
Hoo… the fog came in. Everything looks soft.

b.say: What do you think fog is?

choices.label: A cloud on the ground
choices.reply: A cloud that came down to visit… how kind.

set.fog: is a cloud visiting the ground

choices.memory: You told me… the fog is a cloud visiting the ground

choices.label: A blanket
choices.reply: A blanket for the whole meadow… a very big blanket.
choices.memory: You told me… the fog is a meadow blanket

choices.label: No idea
choices.reply: No idea… me neither. It's a {word:soft} mystery.
choices.memory: You told me… the fog is a soft mystery

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Hm… I think the world is taking a nap. Fog is the blanket.

c.say: I can't see the trees… but I know they're there. That's a nice feeling.

d.say: {pet_phrase} It'll lift when it's ready… fog is patient, like me.

a.say: Hoo… fog. You said fog {var:fog}.
Foggy morning… the trees are wearing scarves.
Hoo. …Hoo. Did my hoot just answer itself?

b.say: Who do you think hooted back?

choices.label: Another Whimber
choices.reply: Another Whimber… somewhere out there. Hello, friend.
choices.memory: You told me… the hoot came from another Whimber

choices.label: The hills
choices.reply: The hills… they're only copying. Polite hills.
choices.memory: You told me… the hoot came from the hills

choices.label: Your echo
choices.reply: My echo… my hoot went on a little trip. Hoo.
choices.memory: You told me… the hoot was Whimber's own echo

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… maybe it was the night saying hoo, in its own way.

c.say: If I hoot softly… does the echo hoot softly too? …Hoo.

d.say: {pet_phrase} Goodnight, echo. …It said it back. How lovely.

a.say: Hoo. …Hoo. You said that hoot {var:owlhoot}.
Evening hoots carry far… all the way to the hills.
Hm… listen. It's so {word:soft} right now.

b.say: Do you think quiet has a sound?

choices.label: Yes, a soft one
choices.reply: A soft one… like a feather landing. Yes.
choices.memory: You told me… the quiet has a soft sound

choices.label: No sound at all
choices.reply: No sound at all… then it's the only thing with none.
choices.memory: You told me… the quiet has no sound at all

choices.label: It sounds like breathing
choices.reply: Like breathing… slow and kind. Hoo.
choices.memory: You told me… the quiet sounds like breathing

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Well… I'd guess quiet hums. Very, very low.

c.say: If I say 'quiet,' then it isn't quiet anymore… oh dear.

d.say: {pet_phrase} Let's be quiet a while… together.

a.say: …listen. You said quiet {var:silence}.
The night quiet is the softest kind.

b.say: What do you think the window sees all day?

choices.label: Birds
choices.reply: Birds… flying past, saying hello. A busy window.
choices.memory: You told me… the window sees birds all day

choices.label: Clouds
choices.reply: Clouds… slowly. Windows are good at slowly.
choices.memory: You told me… the window sees clouds all day

choices.label: You!
choices.reply: Me… sitting here. It must know me very well.
choices.memory: You told me… the window sees Whimber sitting here

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: …perhaps it sees the sky change its mind. Many times.

c.say: A window is a wall you can look through… isn't that strange.

d.say: {pet_phrase} I'll sit a little longer… the sill is nice.

a.say: Hm… the window. You said it {var:window}.
Afternoon sun on the window… my feathers are toasty.
Hm… one of my feathers fell out. A little one.

b.say: What should we do with the feather?

choices.label: Keep it
choices.reply: Keep it… for the memory book. Soft and grey.
choices.memory: You told me… the feather is a keepsake

choices.label: Let the wind have it
choices.reply: Let the wind take it… off it goes. Goodbye, feather.
choices.memory: You told me… the feather went off on the wind

choices.label: Make it a pen
choices.reply: A pen… we could write very {word:soft} words.

set.feather: is a pen for soft words

choices.memory: You told me… the feather is a pen for soft words

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Hm… I think it wants to float a while. Feathers like that.

c.say: I have lots of feathers… I don't know how many. I've never counted.

d.say: {pet_phrase} It's a good feather. Quietly wonderful.

a.say: …my feather. You said it {var:feather}.
Morning preening… every feather in its place. Mostly.

b.say: …all my feathers are in place. Mostly.

a.say: Well… a warm cup of tea is a nice thing to look at.

b.say: Why do you think tea is so nice?

choices.label: It's warm
choices.reply: Warm… like holding a little sunset.
choices.memory: You told me… the cup of tea is nice because it's warm

choices.label: The steam
choices.reply: The steam… it's like the tea is waving.
choices.memory: You told me… the cup of tea waves with its steam

choices.label: Teapots are fun
choices.reply: Teapots… with their little spouts. They look so polite.
choices.memory: You told me… the cup of tea comes from polite teapots

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… maybe it's the waiting. Tea makes you wait, gently.

c.say: Tea is leaves in water… so I'm drinking a tree? Hoo.

d.say: {pet_phrase} I'll let it cool… slowly. My favorite speed.

a.say: Well… tea. You said it {var:tea}.
Evening tea… the cozy kind of evening.
Hoo… it's very bright. Is the sun always this… loud?

b.say: What do you say to the sun in the morning?

choices.label: Good morning
choices.reply: Good morning, sun… you're very early.

set.sunrise: gets a good morning from us

choices.memory: You told me… the sunrise gets a good morning from us

choices.label: Rise and shine
choices.reply: Rise… and shine? I can rise. I don't think I shine.

set.sunrise: heard us say rise and shine

choices.memory: You told me… the sunrise heard us say rise and shine

choices.label: Five more minutes
choices.reply: Five more minutes… yes. That's what I say too.
choices.memory: You told me… the sunrise gets a five-more-minutes

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Well… I'd guess I'd say 'not yet.' Politely.

c.say: Why don't they just say 'wake up'… oh, good. It's not just me.

d.say: {pet_phrase} I'll open one eye. …The other one is still deciding.

a.say: (Yawn.) …morning. Remember? The sunrise {var:sunrise}.
Morning sun… it's so bright. I'll squint politely.

b.say: Why do shadows get long… at the end of the day?

choices.label: They stretch
choices.reply: They stretch… like me when I wake up. Hoo.

set.shadow_w: stretches at the end of the day

choices.memory: You told me… the shadow stretches at the end of the day

choices.label: They're running home
choices.reply: Running home… to the night. Home is the dark for them.

set.shadow_w: runs home at the end of the day

choices.memory: You told me… the shadow runs home at the end of the day

choices.label: No idea
choices.reply: No idea… a long mystery. Long like the shadow.
choices.memory: You told me… the shadow is a long mystery

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: …perhaps they're reaching for the night. Saying hello early.

c.say: My shadow has no eyes… but it knows where I am. Hm.

d.say: {pet_phrase} It'll go to sleep when the sun does… together.

a.say: Hm… long shadows. You said a shadow {var:shadow_w}.
Long evening shadows… everything is a giant.
Oh… I can hear the river from here. Far, but there.

b.say: Where do you think the river is going?

choices.label: To the sea
choices.reply: To the sea… it's been going there a long time.
choices.memory: You told me… the river is going to the sea

choices.label: To visit fish
choices.reply: To visit fish… every fish, one by one. Kind river.
choices.memory: You told me… the river is visiting the fish

choices.label: Nowhere
choices.reply: Nowhere… just moving. Like humming.
choices.memory: You told me… the river just moves along like humming

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Hm… I think the river doesn't mind where. It likes the going.

c.say: The river is always here and always leaving… at the same time. Hm.

d.say: {pet_phrase} We can listen to it go… it sounds like a long shh.

a.say: …the river sound. You said it {var:river}.
The river sounds louder at night… or the night is quieter.
Hoo… the snow is falling very slowly. Like it's thinking.

b.say: What do snowflakes talk about… on the way down?

choices.label: Where to land
choices.reply: Where to land… a big decision. Take your time, snowflake.
choices.memory: You told me… the snow talks about where to land

choices.label: They hum
choices.reply: Humming… a very {word:soft} hum. Too quiet for me. Almost.
choices.memory: You told me… the snow hums on the way down

choices.label: They giggle
choices.reply: Giggling… because falling tickles. Of course.
choices.memory: You told me… the snow giggles on the way down

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Mm… maybe they don't talk. They're listening to the quiet.

c.say: Each one is different… I wonder if they know.

d.say: {pet_phrase} One landed on my beak… it's thinking there now.

a.say: Hoo… snow. You said snowflakes… {var:snow_w}.
Snowy morning… the meadow is very hushful.
Hm… the lantern is glowing. It's a small, brave light.

b.say: Is the lantern brave, do you think?

choices.label: Very brave
choices.reply: Very brave… one little light in all that dark. Yes.
choices.memory: You told me… the lantern is very brave

choices.label: It's happy
choices.reply: Happy… glowing is how it smiles.
choices.memory: You told me… the lantern is happy when it glows

choices.label: It's a moon friend
choices.reply: A moon friend… down here, keeping the moon company.
choices.memory: You told me… the lantern keeps the moon company

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: Well… I'd guess it doesn't think about it. It just glows.

c.say: Lanterns and moths and me… the night club. Hoo.

d.say: {pet_phrase} We'll leave it on a while… it's cozy.

choices.reply: Yes… just looking is a kind of hello too.

c.say: (Slow blink at the moon.) …There. That one was for both of us.

a.say: Hm… I'm trying to count the crickets by their chirps.

b.say: …one… two… two again… I think that one chirps twice.

c.say: How many do you think there are?

choices.label: A hundred
choices.reply: A hundred… then it's a very big choir. Hoo.

choices.label: Just two
choices.reply: Just two… singing very hard. How brave.

choices.label: @pool:unsure
choices.reply: Mm. Some things are for listening, not counting.

a.say: …the rain is drawing lines on the window. Which drop will win the race?

choices.label: That one
choices.reply: That one… it's going slowly. Patient drop.

choices.label: The fast one
choices.reply: The fast one… oh, it joined another. Now they're one drop.

b.say: Nobody won… they all got to the bottom. That seems fair.

a.say: Hoo… there's a little cluster of stars I haven't named.

choices.label: The Teapot
choices.reply: The Teapot… yes. I can see the spout.
choices.memory: We named some stars the Teapot

choices.label: The Snail
choices.reply: The Snail… a slow star. My kind of star.
choices.memory: We named some stars the Snail

choices.label: The Sock
choices.reply: The Sock… someone's lost sock. In the sky. Hoo-hoo.
choices.memory: We named some stars the Sock

c.say: {pet_phrase} I'll say goodnight to {var:starName}… quietly, when it comes out.

a.say: Well… I tried to turn a page with my talons. Three pages turned.

b.say: Shall we read the page we landed on?

choices.label: @pool:yes
choices.reply: (Peers.) …It says "the." Just "the." A very short page.

choices.label: Go back
choices.reply: Back… (Flaps the pages.) Now we're at the start. Hoo.

c.say: Reading is slow for Whimbers. I like slow.

a.say: (Feathers flutter.) …The wind is combing my feathers the wrong way.

choices.label: Very!
choices.reply: Very ruffled… hoo-hoo. A windy Whimber.

choices.label: A little
choices.reply: A little… I'll fluff and settle. (Fluffs.) There.

choices.label: So cozy!
choices.reply: Cozy… I'll take cozy. Thank you.

a.say: Hm… the moth is going around and around the lantern.

b.say: Shall we dance like a moth?

choices.label: @pool:yes
choices.reply: (Turns in a slow circle.) …I'm a very slow moth. A careful moth.

choices.label: @pool:no
choices.reply: All right… we'll be the audience. Very quiet clapping.

a.say: Oh… one dew drop is holding the whole sun inside it.

b.say: Shall I drink it or leave it?

choices.label: Drink it
choices.reply: (Sips.) …It tasted like morning. Cool and green.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.reply: Leave it… yes. It looks happy there. Sparkling.

a.say: Hoo… the fog is so thick, the old tree is gone. Just gone.

b.say: Where do you think it went?

choices.label: It's still there
choices.reply: Still there… I believe you. Trees are very good at staying.

choices.label: Inside the fog
choices.reply: Inside the fog… having a {word:soft} rest.

c.say: When the fog lifts… hello again, tree.

a.say: Hm… I've been working on a hoot song. It has two notes.

c.say: Did you like it?

choices.label: Encore
choices.reply: Again… hoo… hoo-oo. (Bows a little.) Thank you.

choices.label: Add a note
choices.reply: A third note… hoo… hoo-oo… hee. Oh. That was new.

choices.label: @pool:giggle
choices.reply: Hoo-hoo… I like that you giggled. That's a good review.

b.say: (Tilts head.) …I hear a leaf settling. A very small leaf.

c.say: What do you hear?

choices.label: Breathing
choices.reply: Breathing… soft and slow. Yes. That's a {word:soft} sound.

choices.label: A bird
choices.reply: A bird… far away. You have very good ears.

choices.label: Nothing
choices.reply: Nothing… then you won. Nothing is the smallest sound.

a.say: (Breathes on the window.) …A little cloud. On the glass.

b.say: Shall I draw something in it?

choices.label: A moon
choices.reply: (Draws with a talon.) …A moon. A bit lumpy. A lumpy moon.

choices.label: A smile
choices.reply: (Draws.) …A smile. The window looks happy now.

choices.label: A star
choices.reply: (Draws.) …A star. Five points. I think. Maybe four.

choices.label: Your name
choices.reply: (Draws a squiggle.) …That says "Whimber." In Whimber.

choices.label: Goodnight
choices.reply: (Writes slowly.) …"Goodnight." It's very wobbly. Wobbly goodnight.

choices.label: Wait more
choices.reply: Wait more… yes. (Waits.) …(Still waiting.) …Hoo.

choices.reply: One… (Opens one.) There. Half a morning. Just right.

choices.label: Both eyes
choices.reply: Both… (Opens both.) Oh. So much morning. Hoo.

choices.label: Close them
choices.reply: Close them… (Closes.) Mm. Morning can wait a little.

c.say: {pet_phrase} It's only borrowing my shape… it gives it back when I fold up.

b.say: Where would the leaf go first?

choices.label: Past a frog
choices.reply: Past a frog… who says hello. Ribbit. Very polite river.

choices.label: Under a bridge
choices.reply: Under a bridge… into the shade, and out again.

choices.label: All the way to the sea
choices.reply: All the way… what a long journey for one small leaf.

b.say: Shall I walk in a circle?

choices.label: @pool:yes
choices.reply: (Walks slowly around.) …A fork circle. Hoo. A snow picture.

choices.label: Hop instead
choices.reply: (Hops.) …Two forks at a time. Very tidy.

choices.label: You
choices.reply: Me… (fluffs up very round). Oh. Thank you. Hoo.

choices.label: The books
choices.reply: The books… they look like they're glowing with stories.

choices.label: The teapot

choices.reply: For the memory book… then I'll remember today. Pinecone day.

choices.label: Back to the tree
choices.reply: Back near the tree… yes. Its family is there.

choices.label: Blink
choices.reply: (Slow blink.) …(Blink.) …I'm a very slow firefly.

choices.label: Count them

choices.label: @pool:listen
choices.reply: (Still and quiet.) …They don't make a sound. Lights only. Lovely.

b.say: Shall we see who's slower… me or the cloud?

choices.label: You!
choices.reply: (Moves one feather.) …Slowly… slowly… I think I win.

choices.label: The cloud
choices.reply: The cloud… yes. It's had more practice.

choices.label: The red one
choices.reply: (Reaches.) …Missed. It went around me. Clever leaf.

choices.label: The big one
choices.reply: (Opens wings.) …Caught. It landed right in my feathers.

choices.label: Any of them
choices.reply: Any… (one lands on its head). …Hoo. It caught me.

a.say: Hoo… once upon a time, there was a teacup.

choices.label: To see the sea
choices.reply: To see the sea… so it rolled very carefully to the river.

choices.label: More tea
choices.reply: More tea… so it asked the teapot nicely.

choices.label: To visit the moon
choices.reply: To visit the moon… so it waited for a full one.

choices.reply: Pink… the shy part. Like a blush.

choices.label: Purple

choices.label: Blue

choices.label: Slow

choices.label: A feather
choices.reply: A feather… of course. Soft and familiar.

choices.label: A bit of yarn

choices.label: A star
choices.reply: A star… I'd have to ask nicely. Hoo-hoo.

c.say: {pet_phrase} Snuffle friends. I'm glad we met.

choices.label: Leave it

choices.reply: Me… hello, caterpillar. Through your window.

choices.reply: A tea party… mushroom chairs. Lovely.
